feedback.problem: What is the coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-{x}^{3}}$ at $x=1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=1$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1)+\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is

$$
\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(1).
$$

$$

$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-{x}^{3}} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-{x}^{2}{e}^{-{x}^{3}} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-2x{e}^{-{x}^{3}}+3{x}^{4}{e}^{-{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1) & =-2\cdot 1\cdot {e}^{-{1}^{3}}+3\cdot {1}^{4}\cdot {e}^{-{1}^{3}} \\  & =-2{e}^{-1}+3{e}^{-1} \\  & ={e}^{-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x-1)^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2} & =\frac{{e}^{-1}}{2}=\frac{1}{2e}\end{aligned}
$$
